changedFiles.change: hardened runner: in-consumer AOT source (P1R-01); ngc --traceResolution provenance proof (P1R-02); negative-control sabotage gate (P1R-03); explicit resolution-vs-runtime classification (P1R-04); consumable repeat-pack install+resolve (P1R-05); maxBuffer fix for >1MB trace

weaknessesCorrected.weakness: AOT compiled the component from the repo source dir, so compile-time resolution could pick the workspace dist (via the S4 symlink) rather than the installed tarball
weaknessesCorrected.correction: Copy component into the isolated consumer's src/; add --traceResolution and assert resolution provenance (installed node_modules vs repo dist)

weaknessesCorrected.weakness: ESM import catch swallowed any exception (only ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND flagged)
weaknessesCorrected.correction: Separate resolution (hard assert) from runtime; runtime must be full success or a SPECIFIC known Angular-JIT error matched by message

weaknessesCorrected.weakness: 2nd tarball only checked 3 manifest fields, not actual consumability
weaknessesCorrected.correction: Install 2nd tarball into a fresh consumer and resolve it; also assert each export target exists inside it

harnessFix.issue: ngc --traceResolution emits >1MB on stdout; Node spawnSync default maxBuffer (1MB) SIGTERM-killed the child mid-write, producing a spurious non-zero status and a missing output file (which cascaded into a boot failure).
harnessFix.evidence: Isolated repro: spawnSync default buffer -> status=null, signal=SIGTERM, no .aot-out emitted; with maxBuffer=256MB -> status=0, .aot-out/consumer-app.component.js emitted, boot OK.

provenanceProof.method: component copied to <consumer>/src; tsconfig inside consumer (rootDir ./src); ngc -p tsconfig --traceResolution run with cwd=consumer

negativeControl.method: copy installed package to scratch consumer; remove dist/types; delete exports/types/module from manifest; run identical ngc compile
negativeControl.purpose: prove the AOT gate is sensitive to losing the package's exports/declarations and is not a false positive

resolutionVsRuntime.resolution: import.meta.resolve and require.resolve must both succeed and point at the INSTALLED tarball (.../consumer/node_modules/@smilodon/angular/...), never repo dist — hard assertions
resolutionVsRuntime.runtime: structured result; runtime must be IMPORTED_KEYS=… (full success) OR THREW:… matching KNOWN_JIT = /needs to be compiled using the JIT compiler|@angular\/compiler/i; any other exception fails the gate

checks: every export target physically exists inside the 2nd tarball
2nd tarball installed into a fresh consumer and import.meta.resolve succeeds
